title: Oridonin exposure induces testicular impairment through regulating ferroptosis via HIF-1alpha/HO-1 activation and STUB1-driven GPX4 ubiquitination-dependent degradation.
authors: Xu, Zhongchi; Li, Jiaqi; Hou, Yuyang; Deng, Zhewen; Zhang, Qi; Ma, Bo
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Oridonin通过铁死亡通路致睾丸损伤的毒理机制，涉及蛋白泛素化与信号通路，但无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Oridonin (ORI), a bioactive diterpenoid isolated from Rabdosia rubescens, possesses anti-inflammatory, antibacterial and anti-tumor medicinal properties. However, its clinical application has been limited due to significant male reproductive toxicity, the underlying mechanisms of which remain elusive. In this study, we explore the potential mechanism of ORI-induced testicular injury and identify potential therapeutic targets for mitigating its reproductive toxicity. GC-MS metabolomics was employed to investigate differential metabolites in the serum of mice subjected to ORI-induced testicular injury. we demonstrated for the first time in vivo and in vitro that ORI-induced testicular ferroptosis, accompanied by cysteine, GSH and NADPH depletion, ROS accumulation, intracellular ferrous enrichment, and changes in the expression of ferroptosis-related proteins. Molecular docking and co-immunoprecipitation (CO-IP) were performed to validate the STUB1-GPX4 interaction and GPX4 ubiquitination. Network toxicology identified potential targets, followed by experimental validation of HIF-1alpha/HO-1 pathway activation via Western blot, RT-qPCR, and immunohistochemistry (IHC). Mechanistically, ORI induced testicular ferroptosis through two distinct pathways: (1) STUB1-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of GPX4, and (2) activation of the HIF-1alpha/HO-1 signaling axis, as predicted by network toxicology and confirmed experimentally. Collectively, this study provides the first evidence that ORI exposure induces testicular impairment via dual mechanisms: HIF-1alpha/HO-1 pathway activation and STUB1-dependent GPX4 ubiquitination, both of which collectively facilitate ferroptosis. These findings not only elucidate the molecular basis of ORI induced-reproductive toxicity but also identify STUB1 and HIF-1alpha/HO-1 as potential therapeutic targets for prevention and treatment.
abstract_zh: 冬凌草甲素（Oridonin, ORI）是从碎米桠（Rabdosia rubescens）中分离的一种生物活性二萜类化合物，具有抗炎、抗菌和抗肿瘤的药用特性。然而，由于其显著的雄性生殖毒性，其临床应用受到限制，而其潜在机制仍不明确。在本研究中，我们探讨了ORI诱导睾丸损伤的潜在机制，并确定了减轻其生殖毒性的潜在治疗靶点。采用气相色谱-质谱联用代谢组学（GC-MS metabolomics）方法，研究ORI诱导睾丸损伤小鼠血清中的差异代谢物。我们首次在体内和体外证明，ORI诱导的睾丸铁死亡（ferroptosis）伴随半胱氨酸、谷胱甘肽（GSH）和烟酰胺腺嘌呤二核苷酸磷酸（NADPH）耗竭、活性氧（ROS）积累、细胞内亚铁富集以及铁死亡相关蛋白表达的变化。通过分子对接和免疫共沉淀（co-immunoprecipitation, CO-IP）验证了STUB1-GPX4相互作用及GPX4泛素化。网络毒理学确定了潜在靶点，随后通过蛋白质印迹（Western blot）、实时定量聚合酶链反应（RT-qPCR）和免疫组织化学（IHC）实验验证了缺氧诱导因子-1α/血红素加氧酶-1（HIF-1alpha/HO-1）通路的激活。在机制上，ORI通过两条不同途径诱导睾丸铁死亡：（1）STUB1介导的GPX4泛素化和降解，以及（2）HIF-1alpha/HO-1信号轴的激活，后者由网络毒理学预测并经实验证实。总体而言，本研究首次提供证据表明，ORI暴露通过双重机制诱导睾丸损伤：HIF-1alpha/HO-1通路激活和STUB1依赖性GPX4泛素化，两者共同促进铁死亡。这些发现不仅阐明了ORI诱导生殖毒性的分子基础，还将STUB1和HIF-1alpha/HO-1确定为预防和治疗的潜在治疗靶点。
